content.text:
IPv6 literals in link destinations now keep their brackets. `[visit](http://[2001:db8::1]/)` should now render `href="http://[2001:db8::1]/"`.

I checked `http://[::1]/` through the rebuilt `dist` and it gave `href="http://[::1]/"`. I didn't run the exact example from your report. My test with a port also had a space in the URL, so it wasn't a valid link and proved nothing. The existing `test/markdown-it` suite passes (300 tests, 0 failures). I didn't add a regression test, and I didn't run lint, type-check, or the other test suites from `npm test`.

**Cause:** `normalizeLink` in `src/markdownit.ts` parses the URL, rebuilds it (which wraps an IPv6 host in `[` `]`), then runs `mdurl.encode` on the whole string. That encode step percent-encodes the brackets.

**Fix:** when the parsed hostname contains `:`, `normalizeLink` swaps in a placeholder host. It encodes the rest of the URL as before, then puts the bracketed host back in. The path, query, and every other URL are encoded as they were before.
